title: Nebuchadnezzar stood on the roof, looked over Babylon, and said:
paragraphs: Nebuchadnezzar stood on the roof, looked over Babylon, and said:
“Is not this great Babylon, that I have built… by my mighty power… for the glory of my majesty?” — Daniel 4:30
That was not confidence.
That was worship.
Of self.
And before the applause finished echoing, heaven answered.

God saw it.
The pride.
The self-glory.
The throne built inside his chest.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

God does not need to destroy a leader to humble him.
Sometimes He simply lets him see what he really is without grace.
“You knew.”

You knew the gift was not yours.
You knew the platform was mercy.
You knew the influence was borrowed breath.
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” — James 4:6
Read that again.

The danger is not leadership.
The danger is forgetting the Lord who allowed you to lead.
Nebuchadnezzar lost his mind because pride had already taken his heart.
And some leaders today are still standing, still speaking, still winning… but heaven has already weighed the throne.
The Gospel breaks this madness.

Jesus, the true King, had all glory and stepped down.
He humbled Himself to the cross.
He bore our sin.
He rose in victory.

Salvation is not for people who build their own Babylon.
It is for sinners who repent and bow before Christ.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
Leader, influencer, pastor, parent, creator—hear this:

Your crown is not proof you are untouchable.
Your success is not proof you are righteous.
Your platform is not proof God approves of your pride.
Repent before mercy becomes discipline.
